eyebrow: Localize the exact op, or assert cheaply every step
code:
torch.autograd.set_detect_anomaly(True)   # expensive -- debugging only
loss.backward()   # raises at the exact op that produced the NaN

# Cheap always-on alternative:
if not torch.isfinite(loss):
    raise RuntimeError(f"Non-finite loss at step {step}: {loss.item()}")
caption: Anomaly detection names the culprit op directly, instead of letting a NaN silently flow through dozens of downstream ops.

eyebrow: Mixed precision needs loss scaling and clipping
code:
scaler = torch.cuda.amp.GradScaler()
with torch.cuda.amp.autocast():
    loss = compute_loss(model, batch)

scaler.scale(loss).backward()     # scale up -- avoid fp16 underflow
scaler.unscale_(optimizer)
torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_norm=1.0)
scaler.step(optimizer)            # skips the step if Inf/NaN found
scaler.update()
caption: fp16's narrow exponent range lets small gradients underflow to zero before the loss itself looks wrong -- loss scaling is the standard fix.
